title: Boss: Gradebook
summary: Objects, destructuring, spread, array methods, sorting and Map together.

steps.title: The job
body: A teacher's gradebook arrives as JSON. You will parse it, compute averages, rank students and group them, without mutating anything you are given.

steps.title: Parse and average
prompt: Write `parse(json: string): Student[]` that parses the JSON array and adds an `average` to each student (the mean of `scores`, rounded to 1 decimal place as a number; `0` when there are no scores). Keep every other property.
starter: type Student = { name: string; class: string; scores: number[]; average: number };
solution: type Student = { name: string; class: string; scores: number[]; average: number };
const sum = r.scores.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
template: Dojo.eq("one student", [{ name: "Ada", class: "A", scores: [90, 85], average: 87.5 }], parse('[{"name":"Ada","class":"A","scores":[90,85]}]'));
hints: Guard the empty array before dividing.

steps.title: Rank
steps.prompt: Add `rank(students: Student[]): string[]` returning lines like `"1. Ada (87.5)"`, highest average first, ties by name. Do not mutate the input. Keep `parse` from the previous step.
starter: type Student = { name: string; class: string; scores: number[]; average: number };
solution: type Student = { name: string; class: string; scores: number[]; average: number };
template: Dojo.eq("ranked lines", ["1. Ada (87.5)", "2. Al (70)", "3. Bo (70)"], rank(dojoS));
hints: `toSorted`, then `map((s, i) => ...)` uses the index for the rank number.

steps.title: Group by class
prompt: Write `byClass(students: Student[]): Record<string, string[]>` that returns an object mapping each class to the names in it, names sorted alphabetically, classes in the order first seen. Use a `Map` while building, then `Object.fromEntries`.
starter: type Student = { name: string; class: string; scores: number[]; average: number };
solution: type Student = { name: string; class: string; scores: number[]; average: number };
hints: `Object.fromEntries(pairs)` turns `[key, value]` pairs into an object.
